title: Daily Market Blog: Inside the Core of the Apple | Investing.com ZA
text:
Vestact Articles (45) My Homepage Follow Yesterday ABSA (JO: ABGJ )'s CEO Maria Ramos announced that she will step down at the end of the current financial year. Unfortunately, the bank's stock soared 6% on the news. Thinking of other cases when this happened, top of mind is when Steve Ballmer stepped down from Microsoft (NASDAQ: MSFT ), the share price jumped over 10%, which added $1.2 billion to his NAV. Not a bad days work, step down as CEO and your wealth jumps by a billion. Returning to Ramos, the question now is where will she pop up in government? Vestact thinks there is a chance she could be Minister of Finance. Time will tell.
Then overnight, the British parliament decided that they don't like the current Brexit deal that took two years to negotiate. Theresa May has been instructed to return to the EU to get a 'better deal'. Shortly after the UK voted, the EU came out to say there is no other deal on the table. Watching this as an outsider, it looks like the UK still thinks they are the world power they used to be. As it stands, the EU holds all the cards. All scenarios are still on the table, hard Brexit, current deal Brexit or no Brexit.
Yesterday the JSE All-share closed up 1.15%, the S&P 500 closed down 0.15%, and the Nasdaq closed down 0.81%.
Company Corner
Michael's Musings
Last night Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL ), formerly the worlds biggest company, reported its Q1 numbers. This will be the first time in over a decade where the holiday season didn't see sales growth. Total sales dropped 5% from $88 billion to $84 billion. Roughly speaking Apple sells $1 billion worth of products every day! Thanks to Apple deploying some of their huge cash pile in buying back shares, 377 067 to be exact or 7% of the company, EPS is at a record high.
Found at BGR
The elephant in the room is that iPhone revenues dropped 15% year over year. This was expected and is why the price of Apple dropped from around $230 a share to the current $155 a share. As the cost of a phone increases and as the technological advances slow, customers are now inclined to keep their phones for longer. What is key though is that customers are still staying in the Apple ecosystem, where there are now 1.4 billion active devices. Tim Cook said the following.
Our active installed base of devices reached an all-time high of 1.4 billion in the first quarter, growing in each of our geographic segments.
That's a great testament to the satisfaction and loyalty of our customers, and it's driving our Services business to new records thanks to our large and fast-growing ecosystem." The services business grew revenue by 20% to $10.9 billion, where Apple disclosed that their profit margin is a whopping 63%! Another division of strong growth is their 'Wearables, Home and Accessories' where revenues grew by 33%. iPhone sales might be slowing but their other divisions are working hard to make up the difference. Even though these results didn't show revenue growth, the share price is up over 5% in after-hours trade. We are still happy holders.
Byron's Beats
Yesterday Shoprite realised a horrible earnings update indicating a 26%-36% drop . Remember their trading statement came out last week which showed very poor sales numbers. Now we are seeing the impact of those poor sales on their earnings numbers. It makes sense when a company is facing increasing costs but sales are flat, earnings are going to decline.
On top of that, they had some issues with their main Distribution Centre in Johannesburg, a strike and teething problems with a change of IT system. I was wondering out loud to Michael whether this was a bit of post Whitey teething pains. Michael said Whitey might have delayed the updating of the IT system, opting rather to stick with 'tried and tested'. It is hard to tell. The share price is currently in an auction, looking to open down 14%, ouch.
I reiterate my point on the retailers. They go through their cycles, Shoprite was the darling for many years. If you had jumped ship from one of the others and bought Shoprite at its highs you would be deep in the red. Rather stick to one quality business (Shoprite included) and ride the waves . You'll probably find that this is a decent long term buying opportunity for Shoprite if you have not yet found your horse.
Signing off
The JSE All-Share is lower this morning. Shoprite crashing by 10% doesn't help. The stock is very volatile this morning bouncing between R149 and R165. It is another busy day today, there is a US GDP read and then the Fed's interest rate decision. The market isn't expecting a change to the rate, but will be paying very close attention to the forecasts for the year ahead. Big companies reporting today are Visa (NYSE: V ), Facebook (NASDAQ: FB ), Tesla and Microsoft. Exciting times!
